caption_en:
Every economy has stars, cash cows and dogs. Here is Israel's.

The BCG growth share matrix (Boston Consulting Group, 1970), applied to Israel's exports:
⭐ Stars: cyber, a record $4.4B raised by Israeli cyber startups in 2025 (YL Ventures), and Google's $32B purchase of Wiz (2026). AI: about 1 in 3 tech investment dollars (Israel Innovation Authority, 2026).
🐄 Cash cows: defence, a record $19.2B in export deals in 2025 (Israel Ministry of Defense, SIBAT).
❓ Question marks: gas, a $35B Leviathan supply deal with Egypt (NewMed Energy, 2025), and food tech: the world's first approval for cultivated beef (Aleph Farms, Ministry of Health, 2024).
🐕 Dogs: polished diamonds, about $7B at the 2015 peak, now at historic lows (Ynet, 2026).

The catch: high tech is 58% of exports (Innovation Authority, 2026). Bright stars, but a lot of eggs in one basket.

Which box would you bet on next? Tell me in the comments.

Photos (Wikimedia Commons): Zvi Roger (CC BY 3.0); Shlomo Roded, PikiWiki Israel (CC BY 2.5); Amir.bendavid (CC BY-SA 4.0); Chenspec (CC BY-SA 4.0). AI voice.

ההייטק הוא 58% מהיצוא. הרבה ביצים בסל אחד.

lines.line: Israel's whole economy, in four boxes.
The Boston Consulting Group matrix. Four boxes, one honest map.
Stars: growing market, big share. Cyber. Israeli cyber startups raised a record four point four billion dollars last year.
Then Google paid thirty two billion dollars for one of them, Wiz.
Star two, AI. About one in three tech dollars here now goes to AI companies.
Cash cows: slow market, big share. Defence. World arms trade barely grew, yet Israel signed a record nineteen point two billion dollars in deals.
Question marks: growing fast, still small. Gas, with a thirty five billion dollar deal to supply Egypt.
And food tech. Israel gave the world's first approval for cultivated beef.
Dogs: slow market, shrinking share. Polished diamonds, about seven billion dollars at the 2015 peak, now at historic lows.
The catch? High tech is fifty eight percent of exports. That's a lot of eggs in one basket.
If you love Israeli facts, follow Noam Roz for more.
So which box would you bet on next?
